candidates.description: The fried chicken magnate and former Governor of Kentucky emerged as the Republican nominee from a deadlocked convention, a compromise between the party's warring conservative and liberal wings. Sanders is a populist moderate with a liberal civil rights record, a businessman's distrust of government overreach, and a promise to bring American troops home from Cuba. He must unite a fractured party while convincing war‑weary voters that a man who built an empire from a single roadside café can restore competence to the White House. His age (74) and lack of formal education invite attacks, but his plainspoken charm have so far turned every weakness into a strength.

The incumbent President is a master of the legislative arena, having passed landmark civil rights and social welfare bills. But his presidency has been battered by an endless war in Cuba, a widening conflict in Indochina, a stock‑market crash, and racial violence erupting in American streets. After surviving two assassination attempts, Johnson is increasingly paranoid and exhausted. He faces a divided party and a strong third‑party challenge from the segregationist right. To win, he must rally the New Deal coalition while convincing moderates that his experience can still guide the nation through chaos.

The Governor of Florida broke with the Democratic Party to run a nativist, hardline anti‑communist campaign. Bryant accuses Johnson of betraying the South on civil rights and Sanders of being a fake conservative. His Heritage Independence Party (“HIP”) promises to crush communism with overwhelming force, seal the border against Cuban refugees, and restore “traditional” racial order. Bryant’s strategy is to sweep the Deep South, deadlock the Electoral College, and emerge as kingmaker, or, president.

Scranton brings youth, executive experience, and appeal to the industrial Rust Belt. A calm and conciliatory figure, he balances the ticket geographically and ideologically, reassuring donors and suburban voters that a Sanders administration will not lurch too far right. His primary weakness is a perceived lack of foreign policy experience, but his handling of protests at home demonstrates a steady hand.

The sitting Vice President is a passionate liberal and longtime champion of civil rights and labor. Humphrey remains Johnson’s link to the party’s progressive base, rallying union halls and minority voters. However, his full‑throated support for integration makes him a lightning rod in the South, and he must defend an administration whose foreign policy has alienated many of his old allies on the left.

The former Governor of Alabama was Johnson’s bitter primary challenger before supporting Bryant. Patterson is a fiery segregationist who frames the campaign as a crusade to save the white South from federal tyranny. His nomination doubles down on the HIP’s regional focus, energizing the Deep South’s most ardent segregationists while ensuring that Bryant’s ticket remains toxic anywhere north of the Mason‑Dixon line.

The senior senator from Maine and the first woman to serve in both houses of Congress. Smith is a moderate Republican known for her courageous “Declaration of Conscience” speech against McCarthyism, her strong support for civil rights, and a hawkish but principled foreign policy. She would be the first woman on a major-party ticket, a historic choice that could galvanize female voters and reinforce Sanders’ independent streak. However, her candidacy is risky: old-fashioned conservatives may balk at a woman in the line of succession, and her dry, serious demeanor contrasts with Sanders’ folksy warmth.

Curtis is a rock-ribbed conservative from the Great Plains, a favorite of the Goldwater wing and a dependable vote against federal overreach. He supported the Civil Rights Act but believes deeply in states' rights, an attitude that appeals to white Southerners tired of Washington mandates without embracing Bryant's fire-breathing segregationism. In the Senate since 1954, he's known as a hard worker who understands the legislative machinery. His plain-spoken, no-nonsense style grates on Eastern liberals but plays well in rural courthouses. Selecting him would reassure the right flank, reinforce Sanders' small-government credentials, and give the ticket a partner who speaks the language of the South and West, though at the cost of alarming moderates.

As the governor of Alabama, Wallace integrated Alabama's schools, pardoned the remaining Scottsboro Boys, and told his state it was time to move on. Now he's LBJ's most effective surrogate in the South, a folksy, combative populist who talks about jobs and law and order, not segregation. He can speak to white Southerners in a way no Northern liberal can, convincing them the Democratic Party still has a place for them. Placing Wallace on the ticket would be a calculated act of political ruthlessness. It would shore up the crumbling South, reassure moderates worried about crime, and weaken Bryant's appeal. But it would also enrage the liberal wing of the party who aren't interested in the south and prefer Humphrey instead.

Also, you would need to drop your current Vice President from the ticket..

Senator Morse is the conscience of the party’s left wing. He challenged President Johnson in the Democratic primaries on an anti-war platform, promising to withdraw from Cuba within ninety days and meet with the Soviets to reduce nuclear tensions. He won the adoration of beatniks, shoutniks, and college students, but not enough delegates to stop the Johnson machine.

Since the convention, he has met with labor leaders and civil rights organizers, positioning himself as the leader of the party's progressive faction. Bringing Morse onto the ticket would be a dramatic olive branch to the anti‑war movement, to Black voters who feel taken for granted, and to union households frustrated with Johnson’s centrism. It would also infuriate Southern Democrats already drifting toward Bryant and alarm the military brass who see Morse as a peacenik.

Also, you would need to drop your current Vice President from the ticket..

The South’s unyielding defender, Senator Thurmond Of South Carolina, abandoned Colonel Sanders to endorse Bryant’s crusade. His presence on the ticket would cement the ticket's focus on more Republican, middle-class, economically conservative voters, and would increase your support in South Carolina.

His economic policies will, however, potentially reduce your popularity with populist voters who usually go for the Democratic candidates.

issues.description: Opinion on the Cuban war and overseas military involvement in general.

issues.name: Immigration
issues.description: Opinions on the Cuban Refugee Crisis and the 1961 reform.

questions.description: The Democratic National Convention in Chicago was a bruising affair. Protesters clashed with police outside Mayor Daley's offices, Wayne Morse supporters demanded a peace plank, and John Patterson backers walked out when the civil rights language was reaffirmed. Now as you stand at the podium as your party's nominee, what is the central message of your acceptance speech?

answers.description: Four years ago I promised to build a Great Society, and I've delivered. Medicare, Medicaid, the Civil Rights Act, the Voting Rights Act. More Americans have healthcare, more children are in school, and more families have a decent roof over their heads than ever before. Our work isn't finished, and I'm asking the American people for four more years to complete it. Don't let the Republicans undo everything we've built.
answers.feedback: You reminded voters what you've accomplished but swing voters who are hurting from the recession and scared about the wars may feel like you're ignoring their present pain to brag about the past. Sanders is hammering the present, and we need to answer that.

answers.description: I know this convention was tough. I've heard the voices of Senator Morse's supporters calling for peace. I've heard the frustration of Governor Patterson's backers who feel left behind. I'm asking all of you to come home. We are the party of Roosevelt and Truman, and we don't win by fighting each other.
answers.feedback: The hard truth is a lot of Morse voters aren't coming back, and a lot of Patterson voters are already with Bryant. You may have extended an olive branch to an empty room.

answers.description: My opponent is a businessman who made his fortune selling fried chicken. He's never passed a budget. He's never commanded troops. He's never negotiated with a foreign leader. He says he'll bring our boys home, but he can't tell you how. He says he'll balance the budget, but he can't name a single program he'd cut.  I ask you on November third: do you want a Commander-in-Chief, or do you want a cook?
answers.feedback: Sanders' lack of federal experience is a genuine vulnerability. But you spent your whole speech talking about him instead of yourself. Voters who don't already dislike the Colonel might wonder what you're afraid of.

questions.description: Hubert Humphrey has been your loyal vice president for four years, but rumors are swirling. Some Southern Democrats have quietly suggested you drop him from the ticket to appease conservatives and win back voters drifting toward Bryant. Humphrey's liberal reputation, especially his passionate support for civil rights, makes him a lightning rod below the Mason-Dixon line. You choose to continue with him, why?

answers.description: Hubert Humphrey is the best vice president this country has ever had. He's fought for civil rights, for working families, and for the dignity of every American. Anybody who thinks I'd throw him overboard to chase a few votes in the South doesn't know Lyndon Johnson. Hubert and I have stood together for four years, and we're going to stand together for four more.
answers.feedback: You've made it harder to win back any of those Patterson Democrats who are flirting with Bryant. Wallace of Alabama might publicly back you, but privately his people are shaking their heads.

answers.description: Hubert Humphrey has been an outstanding partner in this administration. He knows the Congress, he knows the issues, and he's ready to step in at a moment's notice. Different parts of this country have different views on different issues, but every American wants a vice president who's capable and prepared. Hubert Humphrey is both.
answers.feedback: You gave Humphrey credit without making him the face of the campaign, but some would argue that the South is long gone.

questions.description: Vice President Humphrey has announced he is stepping aside “for personal reasons,” and you have named Oregon Senator Wayne Morse as his replacement on the ticket. Reporters are shouting over each other at your press conference, demanding to know whether Morse's strong performance in the Democratic Party primaries forced your hand, and what you intend to do about the accusations that he is too far left even compared to Humphrey.

answers.description: Wayne Morse is a man of conviction. He and I had our differences in the primaries, but I've always respected his passion and his principles. This country is tired of endless war, and I hear that. Wayne will be my partner in pursuing an honorable peace in Cuba and Indochina. He'll also be a fierce advocate for the working man, for civil rights, and for the Great Society.
answers.feedback: You've paired yourself with the most dovish voice in the Senate, and military families and conservatives are already leaving your campaign. You might win California and Oregon in a landslide and lose Texas and the border states. It's a fundamental realignment of your coalition.

answers.description: I picked him Morse because he'll tell me the truth even when it's uncomfortable. That's what a good vice president does. Wayne Morse will make sure the peace movement has a seat at the table. He'll push me, and I'll push him, and together we'll find the right path forward.
answers.feedback: You are still trying to cling on to the moderates, but Humphrey was already pushing the limit for them. It will be very hard to keep everyone happy.

questions.description: Vice President Humphrey has announced he is stepping aside “for personal reasons,” and you have named Alabama Governor George Wallace as his replacement on the ticket. Reporters are shouting over each other at your press conference, demanding to know whether you forced Humphrey out, whether his anti‑war opinions was the cause, and what Wallace’s role will be.

answers.description: Hubert Humphrey is a good man, but we have a fundamental disagreement over how to handle the protests and the wars. He wants to appease the folks in the streets. I want to restore order and win the peace from a position of strength. George Wallace believes what I believe: A rioter with a Molotov cocktail in his hands is not fighting for civil rights any more than a Klansman with a sheet on his back and mask on his face.. He’ll be my partner in cracking down on lawlessness and rebuilding confidence in this government.
answers.feedback: Wayne Morse of Oregon indicated that he could potentially run as an independent candidate. Unless you have something up your sleeve, you are in big danger.

answers.description: Hubert made his own decision, and I respect it. He’s served this country with distinction, and he’ll continue to have my friendship. As for George Wallace, he’s a governor who’s created jobs, built schools, and balanced budgets. He’s going to barnstorm through every factory town and farming community in this country and tell working folks that the Democratic Party is still their party.
answers.feedback: Wallace as a jobs‑and‑schools populist is a safe and appealing message.  It keeps the focus on your strongest issue with working‑class whites.

answers.description: We’re in danger of losing the South to these "HIP-eez", and George Wallace is the best voice I have down there. He’s a Democrat who’s proven you can move past the old divisions and win elections on jobs and schools. But I want to be clear: Hubert Humphrey is a hero of this party, and I would not be standing here without him.
answers.feedback: Brutal honesty. Let's see if the Southerners are returning to their Democrat roots despite what the polls are saying.

questions.description: The Democratic National Convention was a disaster for your image. Protesters clashed with police, and when a black student organizer was roughed up during an arrest, a small riot broke out. Now, with the Hosea Williams riots still fresh and new violence flaring in urban centers, the press is calling your party the party of disorder. How will you address this situation?

answers.description: Now, I hear these folks out on the avenue. I hear them chanting and carrying on. They’ve got long hair, they don’t wear shoes, and they think they can bring about world peace by waving a daisy and burning their draft cards. Any jackass can kick a barn down, my friends, but it takes a carpenter to build one. Order will be restored.
answers.feedback: Say goodbye to the youth vote.

answers.description: I understand why young people are angry. They've watched their friends get drafted and sent to die in jungles. They've seen injustice with their own eyes. But burning down a neighborhood hurts the very people it claims to help. I'll enforce the law, but I'll also listen. I'm establishing a commission to study the root causes of this unrest. Justice and order are not enemies.
answers.feedback: Mayor Daley is furious, he wanted a full-throated defense of his police, not a commission. And the hardliners in both parties will call you weak.

answers.description: The real cause of this unrest is years of neglect, neglect of our cities, neglect of our schools, neglect of the poor. The Republicans have fought every Great Society program I've proposed, and now they act surprised when desperation boils over. I'm going to double down on the War on Poverty, create jobs in these communities, and prove that the ballot is more powerful than the brick.
answers.feedback: it sounds like you're making excuses for rioters, and the 'root causes' argument doesn't play well in suburban living rooms where people are just scared. Sanders and Bryant is going to hammer you for being soft on crime.

questions.description: Wayne Morse is back. The anti-war Oregon senator who challenged you in the primaries has been meeting quietly with labor leaders and civil rights organizers. Word is he’s preparing to launch an independent campaign, arguing that your move to the right with Wallace and your crackdown on protests have betrayed the party’s soul. He hasn’t filed yet, but his supporters are circulating petitions in Oregon, California, and Wisconsin. Your advisors say he could siphon off just enough liberal votes to hand the election to Sanders.

answers.description: So now I have beatniks on the left calling me an oppressor abroad, and hippies on the right calling me an oppressor at home. Thank God for the moderates – they’re quiet, but they’re the ones that actually vote. Bring it on!
answers.feedback: Ironically Morse could siphon more votes from Colonel rather than spoiling you at this point.

answers.description: I’ll meet with Wayne tonight if he’s willing. I hear what he’s saying, and I hear the folks who are marching in the streets. Maybe I’ve been too hard on the protesters. Maybe I need to be clearer about bringing these wars to an end. Wayne Morse is a man of principle, and I respect that. If he wants to work with me instead of against me, my door is open.
answers.feedback: You finally convinced Wayne after promising huge concessions, but this risks alienating the conservatives and southerners you tried to court with Wallace. Your advisors are wondering if you should have just stuck with Humphrey instead.

answers.description: The difference between cannibals and liberals is that cannibals only eat their enemies... Wayne Morse ran against me in the primaries and he lost. Now he wants to play spoiler because he didn’t get his way. I’ve got a country to run and a campaign to win, so George Wallace is going to go out there and tell the American people exactly what’s at stake: a choice between law and order under this ticket, or chaos under the Republicans and their beatnik allies.
answers.feedback: You positioned yourself politically  to the right of Sanders and Morse started his campaign immediately.

questions.description: Farris Bryant's candidacy is surging. Polls show him leading in Florida, Mississippi, Alabama, and South Carolina, and he's competitive in Georgia and Louisiana. Your own campaign manager warns that if Bryant sweeps the Deep South and deadlocks the Electoral College, the election could be thrown to the House of Representatives.

answers.description: Farris Bryant is just a little barking dog trying to get a headline. He can shout about immigrants all he wants, but he's not going to win a single state north of the Mason-Dixon line. I'm going to focus on the states that actually decide presidential elections. Let Bryant and Sanders fight over the scraps in Dixie.
answers.feedback: Southern Democrats who've been loyal to you for years will feel abandoned. Some of them may sit this one out, and that could hurt down-ballot. Also, if Bryant sweeps too many electoral votes, you might regret leaving the field to him.

answers.description: Texas isn't going anywhere, and neither are the border states where folks know me and know what I've delivered. I've brought roads, schools, and hospitals to communities that never had them. I'm going to spend the fall reminding voters in Texas, Arkansas, Oklahoma, and Missouri that Lyndon Johnson has never forgotten where he came from.
answers.feedback: Bryant is campaigning hard in these states too, and some rural whites are listening. You'll have to work for every vote, and you'll be spending time in Texas when you could be shoring up Pennsylvania.

answers.description: I know the heart of the South. I am a part of it. It is a heart of deep faith, of love for neighbor, and of open-door hospitality. I will focus on the South and I will win it. We will campaign there with Governor George Wallace.
answers.feedback: Governor Wallace is the best surrogate you've got in the South, and this strategy reminds folks why. He's popular, he's been loyal, and his message of 'move on from segregation' undercuts Bryant. The risk is that his presence on the trail could agitate northern liberals who already think you're too cozy with the old guard.

questions.description: The Republican convention in San Francisco was a spectacle: delegates nearly brawling on the floor, vegetables thrown at Goldwater and Rockefeller, and five ballots before Sanders emerged as the exhausted compromise. Your political team has been studying the fallout, and it's clear that neither the Goldwater conservatives nor the Rockefeller liberals are fully satisfied. How do you plan to use that to your advantage?

answers.description: Nelson Rockefeller is a decent man, and a lot of his supporters are reasonable folks who look at what's happening in their party and want no part of it. They believe in fiscal responsibility, but they also believe government has a role to play in helping people. That sounds a lot like what I've been doing for four years.
answers.feedback: Reaching out to the Rockefeller wing is smart politics. Those are the exact suburban moderates we need in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Ohio.

answers.description: Barry Goldwater is a man of conviction, and I respect that. His people wanted a real conservative who'd stand up to communism and cut the size of government. I've been tough on the Communists in Cuba and Vietnam. I've also been a miser with the taxpayers' money, just ask anybody who's ever tried to get a nickel out of Lyndon Johnson. Those Goldwater folks and I have more in common than they might think.
answers.feedback: You're praising the man who called Social Security a fraud and voted against the Civil Rights Act. What can I say? Bold words.

answers.description: I watched that convention, and I'll tell you what I saw: a party that can't even agree on who should lead it, let alone how to lead the country. They threw vegetables at each other. Vegetables! You can't make this stuff up. They spent four days proving they can't govern themselves, and now they want the American people to hand them the keys to the White House?
answers.feedback: Sometimes the best move is just to stay out of the way and let the other guy keep talking.

questions.description: The headlines this morning are grim: a Cam bomb in Boyeros, Cuba, killed 17 civilians and wounded dozens more. It's the deadliest attack on the island in months, and it comes as the refugee exodus from Cuba intensifies. Anti-Castro Cubans are streaming into Florida by the thousands, and Governor Bryant is using the crisis to paint you as weak and the refugees as a threat. Your own intelligence briefings warn that Communist agents could be slipping in among the genuine asylum seekers. How do you stop the terror?

answers.description: We're going to increase security at every port of entry, and we're going to vet every single person who sets foot on American soil. If a man wants to come into the United States, he knocks on the front door, he wipes his boots, and he shows his papers. If he tries to slip through the brush in the dark of night, he is breaking the law, plain and simple.
answers.feedback: Refugee organizations and liberal Democrats are going to howl, and the optics of turning boats away aren't great. On the other hand, you slow down Bryant's momentum.

answers.description: Every Cuban who lands on our shores is a vote against Castro and a vote against Cienfuegos. They're doctors, teachers, farmers who want to work and be free. I'm going to welcome them with open arms, and I'm going to give our military everything it needs to finally root out the bombers who are terrorizing their homeland. The way to stop the terror is to win the war, not to punish the people who are fleeing it.
answers.feedback: That plays well with Cold War hawks and immigrant communities alike. But Bryant's people are already calling you naive, and some Floridians who are scared of the bombings will think you're prioritizing foreigners over American safety.

questions.description: Your campaign team is gathered in the White House for a strategy session. Colonel Sanders, your main opponent, is leading in the polls, his folksy charm is wearing well with voters, and your strategies so far haven't stuck. Your advisors agree: it's time to go on offense, but they disagree on the target. You lean back in your chair and explain to your team:

answers.description: Now, I’ve known some governors, and I’ve known some colonels. Heck, I’ve appointed a few of 'em myself. But there is a wide, deep, dangerous ocean between managing a roadside kitchen in Corbin, Kentucky, and sitting in the Oval Office with your finger on the nuclear trigger. Well, let me tell you something: the presidency of the United States is not a Sunday picnic. You cannot fry up a solution to the Soviet Union. You cannot put a biscuit on the table and expect the North Vietnamese to just pack up and go home.
answers.feedback: The experience argument is our strongest weapon. Voters respect your decades in Washington, and Sanders looks mighty green by comparison. But be careful not to sound like an elitist mocking a self-made man.

answers.description: I want two different messages. In the South, we remind folks that Sanders sided with King, that he forced integration down people's throats as governor, and that he gave money to civil rights agitators. In the North, we tell liberals that he won't even say whether he'd have voted for the Civil Rights Act. He's been all over the map on the biggest moral issue of our time, and that tells you he's either a hypocrite or a coward. Neither one belongs in the White House.
answers.feedback: It could work, but the logistics are tricky. Northern reporters and Southern reporters talk to each other, and if it looks like we're running two different campaigns, the hypocrisy charge could boomerang right back at us. This will also force Sanders to speak up for his civil rights record more, which could ironically hurt us in the North.

answers.description: If you put that man in the White House, Barry Goldwater is the one who’s going to be pulling the strings from the shadows. Sanders is just the smiling storefront. When the bills come due, and when the decisions on war and peace have to be made, it won’t be moderation in the saddle. It will be the same old reckless, trigger-happy, shoot-from-the-hip madness. Don’t let 'em fool you with a fancy coat of paint, a vote for Sanders is just a backdoor ticket to the end of the world.
answers.feedback: While liberals agree with you, Colonel remains popular with most Americans. He's no Goldwater.

questions.description: Farris Bryant has taken his segregationist campaign north, barnstorming through Indiana, Ohio, and even New York. He's drawing big crowds of working-class whites with a mix of anti-refugee rhetoric, law-and-order appeals, and attacks on "Washington fat cats." The latest internal polls show something surprising, Bryant is hurting Sanders more than he's hurting you. Blue-collar voters who might have drifted to the Colonel are now flirting with Bryant instead. Your advisors see an opportunity.

answers.description: Farris Bryant and Colonel Sanders can brawl over the extremes all they want. I'm going to focus on the sensible majority of Americans who don't want to burn the house down or turn back the clock. My job is to govern, not to referee a squabble between a segregationist and a chicken salesman. Let them split the angry vote. I'll take the folks who actually want solutions.
answers.feedback: You're basically ceding blue-collar whites to your opponents and hoping they split evenly enough for you to sneak through. That's a gamble. If one of them breaks out, we could be in trouble.

answers.description: I've spent my whole career fighting for the working man. I passed Medicare, I raised the minimum wage, and I've stood up to the big banks and the big corporations every chance I got. Bryant talks a good game about the little guy, but he's never delivered a single thing for him. I'm going to remind those voters in Ohio and Pennsylvania who's actually been in their corner. They don't need a segregationist telling them who to blame.
answers.feedback: Economic populism is what built the New Deal coalition, and if anyone can reconnect with those voters on pocketbook issues, it's you.

answers.description: Here's the truth: Bryant and Sanders are both Republicans at heart. They both want to roll back the Great Society. They both want to cut taxes for the rich. They're just disagreeing on how loud to say it. I'm going to tell the American people that a vote for Sanders is a vote for the same angry, divisive politics that Bryant is selling with a smile.
answers.feedback: Sanders has a real civil rights record, and his supporters will call you a liar. The risk is that you overreach and end up making Sanders look like the victim of a smear campaign.

questions.description: As expected, the AFL-CIO and every major union have endorsed your re-election. Your choice of Morse as your running mate has energized working-class voters, and your numbers among them are higher than ever. Will you focus on this demographic even more?

answers.description: The AFL-CIO has done more good for more people than any other group in America... It is the labor movement that has fought for the neglected, for the underrepresented, and for the forgotten. We will campaign hard to rally the working class behind our ticket.
answers.feedback: "The American worker is entitled to a fair wage, to safe working conditions, and to the right to organize without fear or intimidation!"

answers.description: I would rather focus on other areas. We've done enough with these rank-and-file fellas.
answers.feedback: Fair.

questions.description: The AFL-CIO and every major union have endorsed your re-election, as expected. But the endorsements from the top don't tell the whole story. Rank-and-file workers are sympathetic towards Wayne, and especially white men in the industrial Midwest are drifting toward Sanders and his talk of "getting government off your back." Some are even listening to Bryant's populist pitch. At the same time, right-to-work states in the South and West are growing, and chasing union votes there might be a losing battle. Your political team is debating where to focus.

answers.description: Now, our Republican friends love to use fancy phrases. They go around preaching about the 'right to work.' Well, let’s call that what it really is: it’s the right to work for less! It’s the right to break a union, the right to tear up a collective bargaining contract, and the right to underpay a hardworking man. I’ll tell you what real right-to-work means. It means an honest day's pay for an honest day's work. It means the right to look your employer in the eye, and negotiate a contract that puts food on your family's table.
answers.feedback: The union brass will mobilize their full machinery for us, and that could make the difference in Pennsylvania and Michigan. But you're preaching to the choir. The workers who are drifting toward Sanders or Bryant aren't going to be won over by a union rally. We might hold our base but fail to expand it.

answers.description: A lot of working folks don't belong to a union, and a lot of them are struggling just as hard as the union members. My Great Society is for every family that's trying to get ahead. Better schools, cheaper healthcare, a fair shake from the government. I'll take that message into every factory town and farming community in this country. Union or no union, a working man knows who's on his side.
answers.feedback: Unions might feel like you're taking them for granted. A little grumbling from the leadership isn't fatal, but we need their boots on the ground in the swing states.

answers.description: This country is changing, and the labor movement is changing with it. Some states have chosen a different path, and I respect that. I voted for the Taft-Hartley Act, and I believe states ought to decide these things for themselves. What I care about is jobs, good-paying jobs that let a man support his family. I've brought more industry and more opportunity to the South and West than any president in history. That's not a union message or an anti-union message. That's an American message.
answers.feedback: Our traditional allies in the labor movement are going to feel betrayed. Some might sit this one out, and that could hand Michigan or Ohio to Sanders.

questions.description: Farris Bryant has challenged both you and Colonel Sanders to a three-man debate in Knoxville. Sanders accepted immediately. Now the press wants to know if you'll share the stage with a segregationist firebrand and a fried-chicken salesman. A two against one pile on could be messy, but skipping it might make you look cowardly.

answers.description: I'll debate both of them. Let Bryant explain to the American people why he thinks segregation is the answer. Let Sanders explain how he's going to end two wars and balance the budget when he's never spent a day in Washington. I'll put my record up against theirs any day of the week.
answers.feedback: Sanders came out ahead, he's quicker on his feet with that folksy charm, and he got more applause lines than you did. You looked like a brawler, not a statesman.

answers.description: I'll debate them, but let's be clear who my real opponent is. Farris Bryant is a sideshow. He's not going to be president. Colonel Sanders is the man who thinks he can take my job, and I'm going to spend every minute of that debate reminding the country that he's not ready for it.
answers.feedback: Sanders still got the better of the exchanges, and some viewers thought you looked petty ignoring Bryant while he jabbed at you from the side of the stage. The post-debate polls show Sanders won. It could have been worse.

answers.description: I've got a war to fight and a country to run. The American people didn't elect me to spend my evenings on a stage with a segregationist and a salesman. They elected me to lead. Bryant can argue with Sanders about who gets to be the runner-up.
answers.feedback: The risk is that you look like you're running from a fight, but some voters respect that you're focused on the job instead of the circus. Sanders and Bryant took part in a one-on-one debate later on and Colonel is considered the clear winner.

answers.description: Bryant wants to look at the American people in the eye and tell them that a man who wears the uniform of this country, a man who bleeds for this country, shouldn’t be allowed to sit at a lunch counter or cast a ballot because of the color of his skin. I want to ask him tonight, right here on this stage: when a young Black soldier is standing in the mud in Vietnam, defending your freedom, does he only have 'states' rights,' or does he have American rights?
answers.feedback: Sanders agreed with you, and the debate descended into a shouting match about civil rights. According to the polls this helped Bryant consolidate his support base while Sanders is considered the clear winner of the debate overall.

questions.description: Internal polls are grim reading. Voters under thirty have abandoned you in droves, flocking to Colonel Sanders and his talk of ending the wars, or staying at home. The graduate school draft deferment repeal was supposed to be a minor policy move, but it's become a rallying cry on college campuses. Student activists are registering voters by the thousands and they're not registering Democrat. Your people are split. Some say you should write off the kids and run up the score with seniors who actually show up. Others warn that losing a generation now means losing them forever.

answers.description: Let me tell you something about young folks. They got passion, and I admire that. But the people who actually decide elections are the ones who've been paying taxes for thirty years and watching their grandchildren go off to war. I'm going to talk to those folks about Medicare, about Social Security, about keeping this country safe. The youngsters can march and wave signs all they want but the grown-ups will decide this election.
answers.feedback: Seniors show up, they trust you on Medicare, and they're scared of Sanders' small-government talk. But writing off an entire generation might hurt down-ballot races where youth turnout matters.

answers.description: I hear these young people. They're scared about the draft, and they're angry about a war that's dragged on too long. I'm angry too. I've already ordered a review of the deferment policy, and I'm working day and night to bring this conflict to an end. But I'd rather have a young person mad at me than dead in a jungle. That's why I'm the one who can end these wars responsibly. I'm asking young Americans to give me a chance to finish the job.
answers.feedback: Some of the more reasonable student types might take a second look, but the hardcore anti-war activists won't be won over by a policy review, and your base might think you're going soft. Still, it makes you look like a president who listens.

answers.description: There's a difference between protest and rioting. Burning your draft card, spitting on soldiers, calling your country a imperialist monster, that's disgrace. My opponent has made himself the candidate of that crowd. He goes to their rallies and nods along while they chant slogans written in Moscow. Well, I'm going to stand with the veterans who fought for this country and the families who raised their kids to respect the flag.
answers.feedback: This could rally a silent majority that's been waiting for someone to say what they've been thinking. Just be ready for the blowback on every campus in America.

questions.description: The Voting Rights Act has been the law of the land since you signed it into law in 1963. For the first time, millions of Negroes across the South can cast a ballot without a poll tax or a literacy test standing in their way. These new voters are a demographic that can help you win crucial states in the Midwest and, potentially, in the South. Will you try to court the Black vote?

answers.description: I passed the Civil Rights Act. I passed the Voting Rights Act. And I’m going to stand on the courthouse steps of every crossroad and county seat and tell the Black population of this country: your vote is your voice, and Lyndon Johnson made sure you have it. We’re going to register voters, we’re going to protect them at the polls, and we’re going to show the world that the Democratic Party is the party of every American.
answers.feedback: Reporters are saying that a record number of Black Americans are registering to vote and are motivated to support you. This can help you a lot.

answers.description: I’m proud of what we’ve done for civil rights, and I welcome every American who wants to vote for me. But I’m running a campaign for all the people, I don’t need to make a special pitch.
answers.feedback: Since they are projected to have a very low turnout in this election, this could be the logical thing to do.

answers.description: The best thing I can do for the Negro voter is the same thing I want to do for every voter: good‑paying jobs, safe streets, and a government that works for them. I don’t need to divide this country by talking about race every day.
answers.feedback: This is a populist answer that will motivate your base.

questions.description: The "Salad Oil Recession" has been a millstone around your presidency: A New Jersey swindler named Tino De Angelis conned banks and brokers out of nearly $175 million by filling tanks mostly with seawater and pretending it was soybean oil. When the scheme collapsed last November, it triggered a stock market panic, a credit freeze, and the worst economic downturn in years. You increased federal spending to steady the ship, but voters are still hurting.

answers.description: I'm sending legislation to Congress next month called the Commodity Exchange Act Amendments. It'll bring real oversight to the futures markets, make sure no con artist can ever pull a stunt like De Angelis again, and protect honest investors from the kind of recklessness that nearly wrecked this country.
answers.feedback: The banking industry will hate it, but it might also steal some of Sanders' thunder on the 'businessman who cleans house' theme. Still, there is plenty of time until next month, and recession continues to hurt families.

answers.description: The real culprit here is the whole Wall Street culture that let that fraud get away with it. The same banks that looked the other way while De Angelis filled tanks with seawater are now pouring money into my opponent's campaign. Colonel Sanders wants to let those bankers write their own rules again. I've spent my presidency fighting for the little guy, and I'm not going to stop now. If you want a president who'll stand up to the fat cats instead of inviting them to dinner, you've already got one.
answers.feedback: This is a good, populist response but voters might notice that the scandal happened on your watch, not his.

answers.description: I acted fast when that crook De Angelis sent the markets into a tailspin. I pumped money into the economy to keep factories open, and I stood up to the Wall Street bankers who wanted to let the little guy take the fall. The recession is receding, and the recovery is underway. Now is not the time to slam on the brakes or hand the wheel to a chicken salesman who's never balanced anything more complicated than a cash register.
answers.feedback: People who are still out of work might not want to hear that the recession is 'receding.' They want to know what you're doing for them right now. Colonel will say you're out of ideas.

questions.description: Colonel Sanders got attacked by a segregationist during campaigning in Dothan, Alabama. He successfully fought off the would-be assassin with his cane. The incident neutralized claims that the 74-year-old man was far too old and frail to be President.

answers.description: Thank God the old man is alright. I mean that. But you listen to me, and you listen real good: Harland Sanders just became the luckiest politician in the United States. We’re running against a living martyr.
answers.feedback: You are right, unfortunately.

questions.description: Integrationist Governor George Wallace has been your most loyal surrogate in the South. He's stumped across Alabama, Georgia, and Louisiana, telling voters that integration is here to stay and that the real fight is for jobs and schools. Now he's pressing you to join him for a series of rallies in Alabama, his home state. "Mr. President, we can lock this thing down," he told you over the phone.

answers.description: I'll campaign with George Wallace anywhere he asks me to. He's been a good governor and a good friend. The South is my home, and I'm not going to let Farris Bryant or Colonel Sanders tell folks down there that Lyndon Johnson forgot where he came from. Wallace and I are going to stand together and remind the South that I delivered for them and I'll deliver for four more years.
answers.feedback: Sounds like the Solid South is back on the menu.

answers.description: George Wallace is a loyal Democrat, and I appreciate his support. But the states that will decide this election are Pennsylvania, Ohio, Illinois, and Michigan. That's where I'm going to spend my time. Wallace can continue making the case for me in Alabama and Georgia, my job is to win the Electoral College.
answers.feedback: Wallace will grumble privately, but the real risk is that Bryant consolidates the Deep South while you're up north, and the Electoral College math gets tighter than it should.

answers.description: Here's what I'm going to do: I'm sending George to Tennessee, Kentucky, Virginia, and North Carolina. Those are the states where his message about moving forward will actually make a difference. I'll keep my focus on the big industrial prizes, but I won't abandon the South entirely.
answers.feedback: Wallace says that you have an even smaller chance of winning these states compared to the Deep(er) South, but obliges nevertheless.

questions.description: Your first term was pretty troubling, but it has some accomplishments like the social programs and the Civil Rights Act. You've got a lot to point to after four years. What's the one thing you want voters to remember when they cast their ballots?

answers.description: I'm going to remind the American people that Lyndon Johnson did what no president before him could do. I passed the Civil Rights Act. I passed Medicare. I passed the Voting Rights Act. I gave millions of Americans the dignity of a doctor's visit and the power of the ballot. When history judges this presidency, it'll be about a president who finally made good on the promise of this country.
answers.feedback: Black voters and liberal Democrats are energized, and this is a good point to remind them.

answers.description: The working man is what matters. I raised the minimum wage. I cut taxes for middle-class families. I created jobs when the salad oil scandal nearly wrecked this economy. The recession hit, and I didn't sit around wringing my hands like others, I acted. Colonel Sanders never had to rescue an entire nation from a Wall Street swindle. I did. And I'll keep this economy growing if the American people give me four more years.
answers.feedback: Pocketbook issues win elections, but in your case it can lost you one because of the state of the economy. Nevertheless, it may still be the safest topic to discuss.

answers.description: The voters know what I've done. What they don't know is what my opponent would do. He talks about getting government off your back, but he can't name a single program he'd cut. He says he'll bring our boys home, but he can't tell you how. He's for civil rights on Tuesday and against the Civil Rights Act on Wednesday. What exactly would Colonel Sanders do if he got into this office? Because so far, all he's selling is a bucket of nothing.
answers.feedback: You didn't give voters a single reason to vote for you, only reasons to vote against Sanders. If this turns into a contest of who's less unpopular, you might not like the answer.

questions.description: It's been a brutal week. A Cam bomb struck the U.S. Embassy in Havana, seriously wounding the American ambassador. Two days later, an explosive report surfaced: American troops may have massacred at least 90 unarmed Vietnamese civilians. Protests have erupted on college campuses, Congress is demanding answers, and your foreign policy looks like it's coming apart. What do you have to say to the American people?

answers.description: First, let me say to the families of those Vietnamese civilians: America is better than this, and I am truly sorry. I've ordered a full and independent investigation. If our soldiers violated the rules of war they will be held accountable. On Cuba, the cowards who bombed our embassy will be brought to justice, but we must not let grief become a license for overreaction. I ask the young people protesting tonight to work with me, not against me. We can end these wars the right way.
answers.feedback: Liberals and anti-war activists are cautious, and the Right is calling you a weakling who apologizes to the enemy. The generals are also privately furious. You make our own soldiers feel like their Commander-in-Chief doesn't have their back.

answers.description: I will not apologize for American soldiers who are fighting and dying to keep the world free. That report is unverified, and I will not throw our brave fighting men to the wolves based on allegations from the enemy. As for the embassy bombing, let me be clear: the animals who did this will pay. I've ordered General Westmoreland to hunt down every last one of them.
answers.feedback: You stood by the troops and promised fire and fury. College campuses are exploding.

answers.description: Let me tell you what's really going on here. Colonel Sanders and Governor Bryant are dancing on the graves of our soldiers for political gain. Neither of them has ever had to make a real decision in their lives. While they're throwing mud, I'm in the Situation Room making the calls that keep this country safe. The American people don't need a clown or a cowboy. They need a Commander-in-Chief.
answers.feedback: It might buy you a news cycle or two while the press chases your attacks, but you didn't actually answer the question, and a lot of voters are going to notice that a president facing two genuine crises spent his time blaming everyone else.

answers.description: I'm seeing mobs on our college campuses spitting on the memory of our fallen soldiers. I'm seeing rioters using this tragedy as an excuse to burn their own neighborhoods. That stops now. I support peaceful dissent, but I will not tolerate anarchy. I'm calling on every American, young and old and left and right, to stand with our fighting men and with the rule of law. If you can't do that, then at least stay out of the way while the rest of us clean up this mess.
answers.feedback: You just called college students 'mobs' and told them to shut up. The youth vote is gone forever, and even some moderate Republicans are uncomfortable. You're betting the whole election on a silent majority that might not be big enough to save you.

questions.description: Vice President Humphrey spoke at a university rally in Minnesota last night, and his words are already making headlines. “We must find a way out of these wars,” he told the crowd. “The young people in the streets are not our enemies.” The anti‑war movement is celebrating, but your Pentagon advisors are livid, and conservative Democrats are privately asking whether Humphrey has gone rogue.

answers.description: My aides keep running in here, hair on fire, telling me that the Vice President just stabbed me in the back on national television. They want me to call up the papers, cut off his campaign funds, and skin him alive. But you know what? I just don't have the bark for it anymore. I really don't. Let him try it.
answers.feedback: Humphrey took this as a sign that you are allowing him to continue making anti-war statements. However, most of the anti-war crowd still doesn't trust you at all.

answers.description: Hubert Humphrey spoke from his heart, and I respect that. He’s been my partner for four years, and he’s earned the right to say what he believes. I share his frustration. Nobody wants to end these wars more than I do. I’ve been working around the clock to find a path to peace, and I’m telling you now: I will not escalate these conflicts further. Hubert and I are on the same page, and we’re going to bring our boys home with honor.
answers.feedback: Joint Chiefs are furious, and your Southern Democrats feel like you’ve abandoned them. At least the Liberals might give you a second look now.

answers.description: Hubert Humphrey is a good man, but he speaks for himself, not for this administration. I’m the Commander‑in‑Chief and I make foreign policy in this White House. I understand that the Vice President is passionate about these issues, but I don’t take my cues from campus rallies.
answers.feedback: You reminded everyone who’s in charge. Conservatives and military families will respect it, but you just publicly embarrassed your own vice president. If you need the liberal base to turn out, they might remember this cold shoulder.

questions.description: Labor leaders are calling your new running mate, George Wallace, a scab. AFL‑CIO president George Meany has privately warned you that several major unions are considering rescinding their endorsements because of the accusations that Wallace is a supporter of nationwide right-to-work laws. You need the labor vote to win the Midwest, but you also need the conservative South.

answers.description: I believe states, including Alabama, have the right to decide these matters for themselves. I’ve been a friend to labor my entire career. I raised the minimum wage fought for collective bargaining, but I’ve never believed that Washington should dictate every policy to every state. The working man can count on Lyndon Johnson. That doesn’t mean I have to agree with my running mate on every single issue.
answers.feedback: Your Southern donors personally came to congratulate you on this but labor leaders feel betrayed.

answers.description: Let me be clear: the economic policy of this administration is set by the President of the United States, not by the state of Alabama. George Wallace will be my vice president, and he will support my agenda. And our agenda is protecting workers’ rights, strengthening unions, and fighting right‑to‑work laws at the federal level. I’ve spoken with Governor Wallace, and he’s given me his word.
answers.feedback: The unions will probably hold their noses and keep their endorsements, but now Southerners are feeling disappointed.

questions.description: There is a problem with your Southern Strategy: The voters that Wallace pulls usually don't come from Sanders, but come from Bryant. While you and Farris fought over voters, Sanders and his middle-class base are up ahead in many southern states. You need to put a stop to this.

answers.description: Let 'em fight over the piney woods. I'm not wasting my time or my money down there. We are going to lock down the North, sweep the big industrial cities, and leave the South to choke on its own tail.
answers.feedback: Fair choice.

answers.description: Then remind those Southern boys that Sanders is a Republican who integrated Kentucky, is in bed with the shoutniks, and wants to let our soldiers die in vain overseas. Slap that civil rights record, along with the others, right around his neck and let Bryant and Wallace chew him to pieces over it.
answers.feedback: Although you are the one who passed extensive civil rights acts, the goal is not to make segregationists vote for you, but to make them not vote for Sanders instead. This will work pretty well.

answers.description: Tell Wallace to stop wasting his breath on Bryant and start throwing his punches at the Colonel. If we want to win the South, we need to go out there and strip the bark off Sanders himself.
answers.feedback: This works to bring Sanders' numbers down, although your advisors wanted something more aggressive.

questions.description: Sanders campaign released ads showing your running mate, Wayne Morse, making extremely dovish statements such as "If I say that the United States is the greatest threat to world peace, I say so simply because it is true." in the context of the Cuban War. Everyone who isn't a diehard shoutnik is furious, and demanding an explanation from you.

answers.description: Wayne Morse speaks for Wayne Morse. I speak for the United States of America. Wayne's got strong opinions, and I respect that. But foreign policy is set me, not by him.
answers.feedback: You tried your best to deflect, but your numbers among the right is eroding, if there was ever any.

answers.description: I don't have to agree with every word Wayne says to be glad he's on this ticket. He's a patriot, and I'm the one who sits across from Shelepin and Castro's people. A little more talk and a little less shooting never hurt anybody so long as they understand who's still holding the gun.
answers.feedback: Are you endorsing his statements? Because it sounds like you are. When did you become a shoutnik?

questions.description: Wayne Morse has been relentless. Every morning he's in your office, urging you to announce a temporary ceasefire with Camilo Cienfuegos' remaining forces in Cuba before the American people go to the polls. A ceasefire now could rally the anti‑war vote, validate Morse's place on the ticket, and change the entire narrative of the campaign. But the Joint Chiefs warn that Cienfuegos will use the pause to resupply and regroup, and your hawkish allies in Congress are already calling any pre‑election deal a "surrender." Aides say the paperwork could be ready by Friday. Will you authorize the ceasefire?

answers.description: Let's get it done. I'll have the papers on my desk by Thursday. Wayne will stand with me at the announcement, and we'll tell the country that the killing is stopping. I've been trying to end this war for four years. Maybe the American people need to see it with their own eyes before they cast their ballots.
answers.feedback: Cienfuegos demands huge concessions starting with the cessation of airstrikes, and his group is refusing to disarm. Still, you have managed to get a temporary ceasefire before the election and Morse is rallying the anti-war crowd to your side.

answers.description: I'm not going to play politics with the lives of our soldiers. If Cienfuegos wants a ceasefire, he can lay down his arms first. I won't hand him a propaganda victory just to win an election. Wayne can disagree all he wants, but I'm the Commander‑in‑Chief, and I don't make military decisions based on polling.
answers.feedback: Morse is extremely disappointed, and he has stopped campaigning entirely until Election Day.

answers.description: Tell Morse I'm still considering it, but these things take time. I need more guarantees from the Cubans, and I need the generals to sign off. If the ceasefire is the right thing to do, it'll still be the right thing to do in November. Nobody's going to accuse Lyndon Johnson of rushing into a bad deal for political gain.
answers.feedback: You managed to keep Morse on your side for now, but public anti-war outrage is intensifying.

questions.description: Colonel Sanders dropped out of school in the seventh grade. Happy Chandler tried to use that against him back in Kentucky gubernatorial election in '55, and it backfired badly. Sanders turned it into a point of pride, and working-class voters rallied around him. Now some of your advisors are suggesting you revisit the issue.

answers.description: Look, I'm not going to apologize for believing that the President of the United States ought to have a basic education. We're hiring the leader of the free world. The Colonel is a fine salesman, but when Shelepin picks up the phone, I want a president who's read more than the back of a biscuit recipe.
answers.feedback: Every working-class voter who didn't finish high school just heard you call their life's work a fry cook's job. Sanders is already out there telling folks you think they're beneath you. This could do more harm than good.

answers.description: I've spent my whole career fighting for folks who didn't have a fancy degree but worked hard and made something of themselves. The Colonel is one of those folks, and I respect him for it. This election is about who can keep this country safe and prosperous. Let's talk about that instead of comparing report cards.
answers.feedback: Sanders can't play the victim now, but some advisors argue that you gave up a chance to attack him.

questions.description: Farris Bryant's campaign is unraveling at the edges. Reports are piling up of his supporters harassing African Americans at rallies, and some of his surrogates have started using openly anti-Semitic slurs from the stump. His poll numbers are slipping in the North, though he's holding firm in the Deep South. You see an opening: a chance to paint Bryant as a dangerous bigot and win back moderate voters who might otherwise stay home.

answers.description: I've spent my whole presidency fighting against hate, and I'm not going to stop now. Farris Bryant has let the worst elements of this country crawl out from under their rocks and call themselves his supporters. Anti-Semitism, racial harassment, this is not what America stands for. I call on every decent American, North and South, to reject this man and everything he represents. You don't have to agree with me on every issue to know that hate has no place in the White House.
answers.feedback: In the Deep South, this might push them further into his camp. Still, you look like a president who stands for something.

answers.description: The American people know who I am and what I stand for. I don't need to give Farris Bryant free advertising by denouncing him every time one of his supporters says something ugly. He's a third-party candidate who can't win. I'm going to spend my time talking about jobs, healthcare, and keeping this country safe. Voters can judge Bryant for themselves without me holding a press conference about it every day.
answers.feedback: Sanders take advantage instead, but maybe this is for the better.

questions.description: Farris Bryant's campaign is unraveling at the edges. Reports are piling up of his supporters harassing African Americans at rallies, and some of his surrogates have started using openly anti-Semitic slurs from the stump. His poll numbers are slipping in the North, and he's losing ground in the Deep South too. You see an opening: Use Wallace to get back these southern votes.

answers.description: I've spent my whole presidency fighting against hate, and I'm not going to stop now. Farris Bryant has let the worst elements of this country crawl out from under their rocks and call themselves his supporters. Anti-Semitism, racial harassment, this is not what America stands for. I call on every decent American, North and South, to reject this man and everything he represents. You don't have to agree with me on every issue to know that hate has no place in the White House.
answers.feedback: In the Deep South, this might push them further into his camp. Still, you look like a president who stands for something, and Wallace successfully fires up the Southern base.

answers.description: The American people know who I am and what I stand for. I don't need to give Farris Bryant free advertising by denouncing him every time one of his supporters says something ugly. He's a third-party candidate who can't win. I'm going to spend my time talking about jobs, healthcare, and keeping this country safe. Voters can judge Bryant for themselves without me holding a press conference about it every day.
answers.feedback: Good. Let him destroy himself

questions.description: The "Lying Lyndon" nickname is spreading. It started with Goldwater's people, but now Bryant's campaign has picked it up, and even some of your own aides hear it whispered at rallies. The charge is that you promised the Cuban War would be over by Christmas 1963. It wasn't. You promised no wider war in Indochina. Then you doubled the troop commitment. You said the economy was sound. Then the salad oil scandal nearly sank it. Will you try to change the public perception?

answers.description: The American people want to talk about honesty? Let's talk about honesty. My opponent has been telling folks he's a simple chicken salesman, but his company was investigated for safety violations. He brags about being a 'self-made man,' but he’s bought and paid for by Wall Street fat cats. The Colonel can’t even be straight about who he is. I’m going to spend the next days stripping the bark clean off him so every voter sees the truth.
answers.feedback: Some of your attacks stick, and media people acknowledge that going on the offensive is a good way to make people forget about your nickname.

answers.description: I don't have time for name-calling. I'm too busy running the country. But I will say this: if the press wants to dig into who's really been dishonest, they might want to take a closer look at Colonel Sanders' franchise operations. Funny how some of his early franchisees ended up broke while he got rich. Funny how he claims to be a friend of the working man but fights union organizers tooth and nail. I'm not saying anything more. Let the reporters do their jobs, and the truth will come out.
answers.feedback: Interesting. Maybe FBI will dig something out.

answers.description: I have made mistakes. I told the country the Cuban War would be over by Christmas because my generals told me it would be. It wasn't, and I've taken responsibility for that. But I've never lied to the American people. I've told them hard truths when it would have been easier to sugarcoat, but I've never run from the consequences, and I've never blamed anyone else. The American people want a president who learns from his mistakes and keeps fighting. That's Lyndon Johnson.
answers.feedback: You just admitted you were wrong about the wars. That's a gift to the Sanders campaign, and they're going to use it, some of your own staff think you just handed the opposition a confession. But most Americans are against the wars, so this could be beneficial in a way.

questions.description: Hoover refused to investigate Sanders, but you campaign people managed to dug up a few things on the Colonel that might be of interest. Which one you will emphasize in attacking him?

answers.description: (A veteran was badly burned by a pressure fryer; KFC was fined for ignorance and forced to improve safety.) A brave American veteran gets mangled by a faulty pressure cooker in one of the Colonel’s kitchens, and his company tries to sweep it under the rug.  If a man is so blinded by corporate greed that he can't even police his own roadside kitchens to keep our veterans safe from being maimed, how in God's name can you trust him with the machinery of the United States government?
answers.feedback: This combines both hawkist and pro-labor vote. Good job.

answers.description: (Franchisees wanted to take KFC public, Sanders refused, leading to threats of legal action.) You see, he loves to preach about free enterprise on the campaign trail, but when it comes down to the ledger, he treats those local store owners like sharecroppers on his personal plantation. He wants all the power, all the control, and all the profit kept right there in his own vest pocket. This is un-American.
answers.feedback: This cuts at Sanders' core identity as the champion of the small businesses.

answers.description: (Sanders acknowledged pressure from federal labor officials over safety standards, because of the dangerous pressure flyer.) That is a direct, cold-blooded attack on the health and safety of the American worker. If a man thinks his private bank account gives him the right to risk the limbs and lives of his own employees every single day, he has no business sitting in the Oval Office.
answers.feedback: Very exaggerated attack, but anything to stop the working-class voters from defecting is justified.

questions.description: It's the last week of the campaign. Your campaign plane is fueled and ready, but there's only time for one more intensive swing through a key region.

answers.description: The South is my home, and I'm not going to let Farris Bryant steal it without a fight.
answers.feedback: It might be too late. The Deep South has been drifting away for months.

answers.description: The Midwest and Mid-Atlantic. This is where elections are won and lost. Pennsylvania's steelworkers, Ohio's autoworkers, West Virginia's miners, these are my people. I passed Medicare for them. I raised the minimum wage for them. I'm going to spend every hour I've got left reminding them that Lyndon Johnson has never forgotten the working man.
answers.feedback: This is the safe play.

answers.description: The Northwest. Wayne Morse country. These folks are anti-war and they don't trust me, but they also don't want a Republican in the White House undoing everything we've built. I'll go out there and make the case that I'm the only man who can end these wars responsibly. If I can flip Oregon, it changes the map.
answers.feedback: Oregon and Washington are small in electoral weight, but they're winnable if you can convince the anti-war crowd that you're serious about peace.

answers.description: Texas is my home, and if I can't hold my own backyard, what kind of president am I? These folks watched me grow up. I'm going to barnstorm through Texas, Arkansas, and Oklahoma and remind them that one of their own is in the White House and that I've delivered for them. If the border states hold, the whole Republican strategy collapses.
answers.feedback: Texas is a must-win.

questions.description: You broke with the Democratic Party after President Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act and failed to stem the flood of Cuban refugees. With that said, most of the populace doesn't know your stance on issues like foreign wars, the economy, and labor laws. What will be the overall theme of your campaign as you rally across the United States?

answers.description: Boatloads of Cubans arrive every week, filling our shelters, taking our jobs, and straining our communities. I will secure the border, halt the refugee wave, and put American workers first. No more handouts for foreigners while our own people struggle.
answers.feedback: This is what your base in Florida wants to hear, but immigration isn't the biggest issue for most Americans.

answers.description: The federal government has no right to tell our states how to run their schools, their businesses, or their neighborhoods. I will defend the right of every community to choose its own path and its own company. Integration has been a disaster, forced on us by Washington fat cats who don't understand our people.
answers.feedback: This message is toxic North of the Mason-Dixon line, but does it even matter?

answers.description: This campaign is for every American who's tired of riots in the streets, bureaucrats in their pockets, and weakness abroad. I will cut taxes, crush the Communists in Cuba and Indochina, and restore respect for the law. You don't have to be a Southerner to believe in order and freedom.
answers.feedback: You've broadened your appeal beyond the South. Law-and-order conservatives, small-government libertarians, and anti-communist hawks across the country could rally to this. Sanders is probably sweating in fear.

answers.description: Our Southern way of life is under assault from Washington elites, radical communist preachers, and an Anti-American 'shoutnik' culture which mocks everything we hold sacred. I will stand for prayer in schools, respect for the flag, and the values that built this country. The South shall rise again!
answers.feedback: The room erupted into a deafening chorus of rebel yells as you finished your fervent speech. Yee-haw!!!!!!

questions.description: You've named former Alabama Governor John Patterson as your running mate. Patterson challenged Lyndon Johnson in the Democratic primaries and has been a fierce critic of the administration. What does John Patterson bring to this ticket?

answers.description: John Patterson stood with Alabama when the federal government tried to ram integration down our throats. He knows the South will not be lectured to by Washington bureaucrats who think they know better than our own communities. Together we will protect our way of life.
answers.feedback: This is a segregationist answer that will motivate your base.

answers.description: John Patterson has been fighting for the working man his entire career. While Johnson sends jobs overseas and Sanders counts his millions, Patterson has stood with the factory worker, the farmer, and the small businessman. He will help me bring prosperity back to the forgotten people of this country.
answers.feedback: You are broadening your appeal to the populist voters across the country. This could be a good plan if you want to undermine LBJ.

questions.description: You've named South Carolina Senator Strom Thurmond as your running mate. He initially rejected the Sanders/Scranton ticket on the grounds that they were too liberal and threw his support behind you, what does Strom Thurmond bring to this ticket?

answers.description: Strom Thurmond has never wavered in defense of the South. When the Supreme Court tried to force integration on our schools, he stood in the doorway and said no. When the civil rights bills came, he fought them on the Senate floor. The South has no truer champion, and with him beside me, Washington will know we mean business.
answers.feedback: This is a segregationist answer that will motivate your base.

answers.description: Strom Thurmond is a United States Senator with decades of experience in national affairs. He's fought against runaway spending, against Communist weakness, and for a strong military that keeps America safe. Conservatives across this country know his name and respect his record. He will help me unite every American who believes in law and order and limited government.
answers.feedback: His Senate record on spending and defense gives you credibility with conservatives everywhere. Just be prepared that LBJ will take advantage of your splitting the conservative vote.

questions.description: The Salad Oil Recession shook this country. A swindler in New Jersey nearly collapsed the stock market, and Republicans claim that President Johnson's spending spree has piled debt onto every American family. Now Colonel Sanders says his business record qualifies him to fix the mess. What is your economic vision for this country?

answers.description: What good is a booming economy if it's built on seawater and lies? The Wall Street fat cats got bailed out while the factory worker lost his job. I'll prosecute the swindlers, break up the monopolies, and make sure the government works for the little guy instead of the big bankers.
answers.feedback: Some of your Southern donors will be nervous about the talk of prosecuting bankers and breaking up monopolies. They might think you're sounding a little too much like a New Dealer. But this is a good way to broaden your appeal to Northern workers.

answers.description: You want to know what's hurting the working man? It's not just Wall Street corruption. It's boatloads of Cuban refugees taking jobs that belong to Americans. It's factories moving overseas while our own people go hungry. I'll secure the border and bring those jobs back home.
answers.feedback: Some voters wonder if you have anything to say about the recession beyond blaming refugees.

answers.description: The federal government is too big, too expensive, and too involved in your life. Johnson has spent us into debt, and Sanders will do the same. I'll cut taxes, slash regulations, and let the states run their own affairs. Free men build strong economies, not Washington bureaucrats.
answers.feedback: Goldwater has called, threatening to sue you over copyright infringement.

questions.description: In the latest years the nation has seen nothing but chaos. The Xenia riots, the murder of Hosea Williams, and now the "shoutniks" burning their draft cards over the unpopular Cuban War, cities are on fire from coast to coast. As the candidate of the Heritage Independence Party, many are looking to you for answers. How would you address these riots?

answers.description: The first thing I'll do is call out the National Guard and give them orders to use whatever force is necessary. These "protesters" are criminals, and they should be treated as such. I don't care if people call me a fascist. At least they won't call me a sissy!
answers.feedback: Whenever you campaign outside the South from now on, you will see beatnik demonstrators holding up posters with slogans like: 'Hitler in 1932, Bryant in 1964' and 'God Bless Farris Hitler, the Smiling Bigot.' They also perform mock-Nazi 'Sieg Heil' salutes at you and your supporters.

answers.description: You want to know why these riots are happening? Because Lyndon Johnson told the Negro he could have whatever he wanted, and now he's angry that the promises were empty. Forced integration has set this country ablaze. Let the states decide their own social arrangements, and you'll see the temperature drop.
answers.feedback: This is a segregationist answer that will motivate your base.

answers.description: I've got no patience for rioters, but I'll tell you something else: Colonel Sanders has been marching with these people. He stood in front of that mob in Kentucky and called it courage. When I'm president, I won't be taking my cues from street agitators.
answers.feedback: Good job, don't let people forget this.

questions.description: Since launching your campaign, your message has resonated with many blue-collar workers in the industrial North, who you seem to be splitting with Colonel Sanders. Do you have any intentions to try and solidify them in your camp?

answers.description: Sanders talks a good game about the working man, but he pays waitresses so little they beg for tips. Lying Lyndon wants to replace the American workers with his Cuban minions. I'm going to remind every factory worker and truck driver that I'm the only candidate who will secure the border, stop the refugee flood from taking their jobs, and put American workers first!
answers.feedback: Your rallies draw big crowds in Ohio and Michigan, even though union leaders are united against you.

answers.description: Let's find the local union leaders who are fed up with Johnson's wars and Sanders' empty promises. Bring them to our rallies and get their names in the papers. If a few key locals flip, the rank and file will follow.
answers.feedback: Only minor and regional union leaders have flipped over to you. While you and LBJ are trying to appeal to the big bosses, Sanders is rallying the rank-and-file themselves. This could help him.

answers.description: Chasing union voters takes time away from the states we're actually going to win. Our path to the presidency runs through the South, not the Midwest. Let Sanders and Johnson fight over the Rust Belt while we lock down our real base.
answers.feedback: Fair.

questions.description: Colonel Sanders has accepted your debate challenge, but President Johnson has refused to share the stage. It will be just the two of you in Knoxville. Now some of your advisors say you should take advantage of LBJ's absence to withdraw from the debate too. Will you still attend?

answers.description: I'm not afraid of a chicken salesman. I'll stand on that stage and tell the American people exactly what I think. Sanders wants to open our borders to every refugee who washes up in Florida. Let him explain that to the cameras.
answers.feedback: Sanders won the debate, but at least you put your name out there.

answers.description: Why should I give Sanders a stage he doesn't deserve? Johnson ducked out, and I should too.  I'll spend that night at a rally with real Americans who already know what I stand for.
answers.feedback: Sanders will blast you for rejecting the debate you offered in the first place.

questions.description: American boys are still dying in Cuba, three years after we were told the war was practically over. Now President Johnson has dragged us into another mess in Indochina, and the casualty lists grow longer every week. Colonel Sanders wants to bring the troops home on a timetable. What would you do differently?

answers.description: These wars were never America's to fight alone. We've propped up "allies" who can't defend themselves and poured blood and treasure into jungles that mean nothing to our security. I'll pull our boys back from Indochina entirely, let the Vietnamese sort out their own affairs. Cuba is different. It's ninety miles from our shores, and we finish what we started there. America first means picking your battles and winning the ones that matter.
